The budget guard charges one token per serialized request byte (an upper bound, roughly four times stricter than chars/4) and treats max_cost_per_call_usd as an operator ceiling, so cost.actual_usd is an upper-bound projection and never an invoice. Seed-receipt spend counts against the live caps; elapsed time is per invocation. The wall-clock deadline does not cover DNS resolution, so manifests should name literal IPs or already-resolvable hosts.

The local lexical control's empty cases run against isolated brains holding one unrelated filler fact (seedbrain refuses an empty brain) and are scored strictly: returning the filler fails. That arm is a control, not the forgotten-fact qualification.

The production lexical fallback (internal/index.LiteralFTSQuery) implicit-ANDs every query term including stopwords, so natural-language questions almost never lexically match a short fact statement regardless of the corpus's designed word-overlap category; the lexical-negative check reads 6/21 in the fixtures run. See embedding-eval.md 'Known limits'.
